To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
, under the assumption that the physical speed propagation of messages is bounded, locality and parallelism combined may yield speed-ups superlinear in the size of the network.

, in the case of networks of processors with local memory, the speed of message propagation is an important parameter in determining the performance of parallel algorithms, and the speedups that can be obtained in these networks can be superlinear in the size of the network.

, in the presence of a physical limitation on the propagation speed of messages, the parallelism and locality of a computation may lead to a speedup that is superlinear in the processor count, even when the number of processors is large, and the computation is performed on a machine with hierarchical memory.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a theory of parallel computing that can be used to design efficient parallel machines.

the development of lower bounds to processor-time and processor-memory tradeoffs, for networks of processors with local hierarchical memories, and with the development of algorithms for such networks.
the design of efficient parallel algorithms for the solution of a large class of problems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in the presence of physical limitations on the speed of message propagation, parallelism and local communication may yield speedups which are superlinear in the size of the network.

, for the models considered, the speedups are bounded from above by the speed of the fastest processor, but are bounded from below by a quantity which is superlinear in the speed of the slowest processor.
the speedups achievable by the use of a parallel computer are not bounded by the speedup of the best known sequential algorithm.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the speedup of parallel algorithms is not bounded by the number of processors used.
, under the physical constraint of bounded speed propagation of messages, locality may yield speedups which are not only linear but superlinear in the size of the problem.
, for the class of problems considered, we can obtain lower bounds to processor-time speedups for any network topology.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the physical limitation on the speed of propagation of messages is a fundamental limitation on parallel computation, and that the parallelism and locality in a network of processors can be combined in such a way as to overcome the physical limitation on message speed.
the speedup of a parallel algorithm is not necessarily limited to the linear regime, even in the presence of a physical constraint on the speed of propagation of messages between processors.
the physical limitation on the speed of propagation of messages can be exploited in order to design networks of processors with high speedup and low communication cost.
